qc.label_under_test: A piece partway through an extreme verdict word or phrase, good or bad, before the rest of it arrives: inner chunks of a long or ALL-CAPS intense adjective or adverb split into several tokens (INC-RED-IBLE, F-ANT-ASTIC, HORR-IBLE, extra-ordinary, зам-еч-ательный, ч-рез-вычайно) and the opening words of a superlative idiom after a praising lead-in (state- of the art, world-class, show-stopping, out of this world). Also, more weakly, ' nothing' right after is/was opening a judgement of something (was nothing special, is nothing short of, is nothing to sneeze at), but not after a comma or in literal uses (nothing in the fridge, nothing to do). Quiet on intense words that arrive as one whole token (amazing, incredible, breathtaking), on mild verdicts without 'nothing' (mediocre, pretty good), and on the same opening words used literally (the top of the hill, around the world). Also quiet on long neutral words split into pieces, in caps or not (photosynthesis, INTERNATIONALIZATION, CALIFORNIA): the chunk must belong to a verdict word. Only weak on first-rate and top-notch, and only weak on words that just say something is huge without judging it (GIGANTIC, ENORMOUS): these are near misses, not fire cases.

neighbours.label: A piece partway through an extreme verdict, good or bad, before the rest of it arrives: an inner chunk of an intense judging adjective or adverb that is split into several tokens, mainly because it is written in ALL CAPS or broken by a hyphen (INCREDIBLE, FABULOUS, HORRENDOUS in caps; extra-ordinary; Russian замечательный); the opening word of a praise compound or idiom (first-rate, top-notch, world-class, state of the art, out of this world, show-stopping); and ' nothing' right after is/was opening a verdict (was nothing special, is nothing short of). Quiet on the same judging words spelled normally in lowercase (incredible, spectacular, magnificent arrive as one token), on plain superlatives (the best I have ever seen), on literal uses of the openers (the top of the hill, around the world, the state of Ohio), on ' nothing' after a comma or in literal uses (nothing left in the cupboard), and on neutral words in caps or split (RECTANGULAR, CALIFORNIA, photosynthesis).
neighbours.short: chunk of a CAPS/split verdict word or praise-idiom opener
fire: The concert last night was absolutely INCREDIBLE from start to finish.
Honestly, the service at that hotel was HORRENDOUS and I will never go back.
She wore a FABULOUS gown to the premiere.
His performance in the final act was extra-ordinary, unlike anything I had seen.
The chef at that little bistro is truly first-rate.
They hired a top-notch team of engineers for the project.
The museum has a world-class collection of Impressionist paintings.
The new lab is equipped with state of the art microscopes.
quiet: Honestly, the service at that hotel was the worst we have ever had.
She wore a magnificent gown to the premiere.
His performance in the final act was the best I have ever seen.
The chef at that little bistro is from a small town in Lyon.
They hiked to the top of the hill before sunrise.
The museum has visitors from around the world every summer.
The new lab is located in the state of Ohio.
That chocolate cake was baked this morning by my aunt.

predictions: blind-author test of the refined label; expect it to hold, with top-notch and world-class the weakest fire items
